title: With "Keep the selection and clipboard the same" option, in some apps the text selection is inappropriately added to the clipboard history *while still dragging*
line: Drag-selecting text in GTK apps, Chromium or Steam now adds one clipboard history entry instead of one per mouse movement.
explanation: GTK, Chromium and Steam update the primary selection on every step of a mouse drag, while Qt apps only set it on release. With selections saved in history, Klipper inserted each partial selection as a new entry; on X11 it used to wait for the mouse button, which isn't possible on Wayland. Now, when a new selection extends or shrinks the previous entry that also came from a selection (its text is a prefix or suffix of the other), that previous entry is removed, after its database write has finished; explicit copies and starred entries are never replaced.

commits.message:
klipper: keep only the final selection of a drag in history

Some clients, like GTK apps and Chromium, update the primary selection on
every step of a mouse drag, so each partial selection was saved as its own
entry. A selection that extends or shrinks the previous one now replaces it.

BUG: 498894

media.caption: Master: a slow 12-step drag selection in Mousepad leaves 12 partial entries in the clipboard history
With the fix: the same drag leaves a single entry with the final selection

review.text: The approach (replace the previous selection entry when the new selection extends or shrinks it) is small and handles GTK/Chromium drag spam without touching explicit copies or starred items, and the DB-job ordering is handled carefully. But with no time bound, a deliberate later selection that happens to be a prefix or suffix of the previous one (selecting 'The' minutes after selecting the whole line) silently deletes a history entry the user wanted. Given two competing MRs (!6460, !6886), this also needs to be presented as an alternative on them rather than a separate surprise MR.
changes: Only coalesce when the new selection arrives shortly after the previous selection entry (e.g. within 1-2 s of it), so deliberate later selections are never removed.
Coordinate with the authors of !6460 and !6886 (link this as an alternative there).
